problems.stem: An AI answer states confidently: "The library closes at 9 PM on weekends." You need this for an assignment. What is the right next step?
options: Use it directly; the answer is clearly stated.
Check the library's official hours page before relying on the time, because fluent wording is not proof of accuracy.
Ask the AI again to see if it repeats the same time.
Add the time to your work and note that AI is usually right.
problems.explanation: Confident phrasing does not make a claim true. Verify factual details against a trustworthy source such as the official page.

problems.stem: Which prompt is most likely to produce output you can actually verify and revise?
options: Act as a peer tutor. List three time-management tips for a first-year student studying 10 hours a week, each in one sentence, and mark which ones you are unsure about.
problems.explanation: A strong prompt names the role, task, audience, format, and even asks the model to flag uncertainty, all of which make verification easier.

problems.stem: An AI gives you a perfect-looking citation: "Reed, J. (2019). Digital Habits. Journal of Campus Life, 12(4), 33-50." You search the library and the web and cannot find this article anywhere. What do you do?
options: Cite it anyway; the format looks correct.
Do not use the claim or the citation, because an unverifiable source may be fabricated.
Change the year to 2020 and cite it.
Ask the AI to confirm the citation is real and trust the reply.
problems.explanation: AI can invent realistic but fake citations. If you cannot locate the real source, drop both the citation and the claim it supports.

problems.stem: You used AI to draft a paragraph with two factual claims. Which verification record best supports a defensible artifact?
options: A note that says "checked with AI."
For each claim: the source you checked, whether it confirmed or contradicted the claim, and what you kept or cut.
The total number of words the AI wrote.
A screenshot of the AI chat with no notes.
problems.explanation: A defensible verification record ties each claim to a checked source and shows what survived. Counts and screenshots alone do not show your judgment.
